summary: Finite visiting takes zero-marked human or place objects and pronominal object suffixes. No Detransitive, new stem or special prepositional sense is established.

Infinitiv zyara/ziyara is retained in the glossary's existing category. Genitive/possessive participants can be visitors (11/111) or visited people (19/2; 68/6), with interpretation supplied by syntax and context rather than one fixed possessive role.
The nominal visitors zayore is already in Part act.; do not infer a separate finite form or new sense.

Repeated add/thin_cell proposals for an already quoted citation, especially 19/2, are deduplicated. The selected 68/6 sentence has a matching translation despite omissions elsewhere in the supplied full verse.

Round 2 only. Jan Beṯ-Şawoce English is project machine translation [MT]; readings rest on the supplied Turoyo. Existing and round-1 wording and numbering are retained. No edition translation is inferred.
The new Detransitive is independently grounded in kmizoro versus active kzayri at the same pilgrimage site. The feminine visited referent is not securely resolved between ziyara and the site.

Finite morphology preserves r-bearing zərle/zərlan, contracted zəranxu/zərənne, expanded zərilox and zayri-/zaryi- vocalisms. No silent r/l normalization or merging with zyr 2 become fat is warranted.
The separated ziyar wo in /5272 and /5274 is not needed to establish Infectum-wa, since zayriwolxu and zayrinawole do so securely.
The cognate i ziyaraṯṯe zərənne is a transparent event noun with its verb, not a new idiom. Ritual visitation is an application of besuchen, already attested in round 1.
Does u qadišano at 11/113 denote the holy man or the sacred site? The edition chooses Heiligtum.
In 68/57, does the genitive ruler denote the visitor to Diyarbekir or the person whom the priest visited? The German resolves it more specifically than the Turoyo alone.
Can editors confirm whether zyara is best retained as the glossary's Infinitiv or separately indexed as the borrowed event noun? No category change is proposed here.
At Jan 2.13/3282, does feminine kmizoro resume ziyara, the monastery site, or an understood feminine noun? Confirm the Detransitive pronunciation.
Explain ziyar wo at Jan 2.32/5272 and /5274 before indexing it as finite Infectum-wa rather than a nominal predicate.
At Jan 2.10/2224, does haykal denote the temple, shrine or statue? The supplied machine rendering statue is retained without settling the lexical noun.
Confirm zarre after d at Jan 2.23/4060 and zəranxu/zərənne suffix segmentation. No new stem or new numbered active sense is proposed.
Jan examples have project machine translations [MT], not edition translations. Editors should check these English renderings against the Turoyo before treating them as vetted translations.
Visited referents include people, places and saint/sanctuary designations; the same visit meaning applies.
Jan supports round-1 extension to people, communities, churches, schools and graves. No separate pilgrimage or school-inspection meaning is established.
Infinitiv ziyara with person suffix and finite zoyarnolxu co-occur in one verse, supporting the prior treatment of visiting nominal and visited participant.
